title: Streaming reliability validation

streaming_unit_tests.command: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_streaming_queue.py tests/test_streaming_ordering.py tests/test_streaming_duplicates.py tests/test_streaming_schema.py tests/test_streaming_health.py -q

streaming_pipeline_parity.note: includes TestParity: all 650 sample events, batch vs stream score-contract columns match at atol 1e-9

redis_5_0_14_1_fallback.note: exercises XPENDING/XCLAIM fallback path (XAUTOCLAIM unavailable on 5.x)

reported_soak_60min.status: verified_against_report_json; consistent with fresh 30s sustained run

preload_drain_ceiling.note: preload=True measures pure single-consumer drain throughput after queue fill; honest ceiling figure

non_preload_burst.caveat: effective_eps denominator is the production window only; post-production drain time is excluded, so this figure is NOT comparable to the preload-drain ceiling and must not be cited as sustained burst throughput

asyncio_queue.notes: bounded asyncio.Queue (50k default); optional JSONL backing with ack tombstones; BackpressureError on saturation; claim_pending respects min_idle_ms

redis_streams.notes: XADD MAXLEN~/XREADGROUP '>'/XACK; XAUTOCLAIM on >=6.2 with XPENDING+XCLAIM legacy fallback; group creation idempotent (BUSYGROUP tolerated); backpressure via XLEN vs max_depth

consumer_groups_xautoclaim.evidence: tests/test_redis_streams.py (8 tests) passed live on Redis 7.4.8 and 5.0.14.1; consumer-restart recovery test confirms XAUTOCLAIM/XCLAIM reclaim of pending entries

pending_recovery.evidence: test_consumer_restart_recovers_pending; worker claim_pending_interval_s=30s sweep in run_worker

checkpoint_restoration.evidence: test_checkpoint_restore_tracker; atomic tempfile+os.replace writes for JSON meta and pickled tracker state; restores tracker state + committed_ids + pending_acks via worker_state

replay_idempotency.evidence: delivery key = (event_id, replay_of); operator replays bypass ingest dedup but downstream committed_ids dedup keeps reprocessing idempotent; test_dlq_write_and_replay, test_replay_of_preserves_duplicate_flagging

dlq_accounting.notes: append-only JSONL DLQ, flush+fsync commit, reason codes (decode/processing_error/late_event/retry_exhausted); benchmark reports dlq_reasons breakdown; events_lost counts only truly unaccounted events

late_out_of_order.notes: per-stream reorder buffers (timed per user, explicit per user+session); emit when event_ts <= max_ts - reorder_window or max_hold elapsed; earlier-than-frontier arrivals -> DLQ late_event; tests/test_streaming_ordering.py 6 tests

batch_stream_parity.evidence: tests/test_streaming_pipeline.py::TestParity.test_stream_scores_match_batch — all score-contract columns match batch analyze_session_intelligence at atol 1e-9 on 650 events

findings.summary: Non-preload burst effective_eps excludes drain time
findings.detail: scripts/stream_benchmark.py computes effective_eps = records_written / production-window elapsed for non-preload modes; drain time after production ends is not included. Burst report stream_benchmark_20261112T040147Z.json shows 410.1 eps which is not a sustained-consumer figure. The preload-drain run (289.1 eps, batch_size=1000) is the honest single-consumer ceiling. Documentation updated to prevent misquoting.
findings.disposition: documented; no code change (benchmark harness behavior preserved to avoid altering reported evidence)

findings.summary: committed_ids dedup LRU is in-memory by default
findings.detail: run_worker dedup of redelivered queue entries uses a bounded in-memory LRU; cross-restart dedup relies on deterministic re-scoring + consumer-side event_id dedup. Documented in code; acceptable for v1.0 scope.
StreamCheckpoint stores tracker state as pickle (atomic write). Version-sensitive; no schema migration. Local-only deployment makes this acceptable; noted for hardening backlog.
Single-consumer ceiling ~289 eps (preload drain, batch 1000). Meeting 500 eps would require partitioned workers or vectorization — explicitly out of scope per roadmap restrictions.
findings.disposition: accepted limitation; carried into CAID_KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md in Phase 4.5

conclusion: All Phase 4.1 verification tasks pass. Reported soak results are corroborated by report JSONs and a fresh 30s sustained run. No architecture changes made. Streaming evidence is consistent and honestly bounded.
